title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside Every Segment — Products, End-Markets & Real-World Examples
question: What exact components does GNA Axles manufacture, what is the revenue split across products, geographies, and vehicle classes, and what does a real-world customer order look like end-to-end?

epigraph.quote: Never invest in a manufacturing business until you can picture the exact part leaving the loading dock, the truck or tractor it bolts onto, and why the buyer cannot easily swap it out.
epigraph.author: Supply-Chain Underwriting Principle

web_blocks.title: Portfolio Architecture: Three Precision Drivetrain Product Lines

web_blocks.html: At its core, GNA Axles does one thing well. It turns alloy steel bars into high-torque, fatigue-resistant shafts and spindles that move power from the differential to the wheels [6][7]. Across Mehtiana and Gulabgarh Jattan, GNA makes roughly 53 to 55 lakh (5.3–5.5 million) parts each year. Part weights span from 1.5 kg SUV shafts up to 165 kg earthmover axles [6][11]. Statutory filings report one auto-components segment. In practice, revenue splits cleanly across three product lines, two geographies, and three vehicle end-markets [1][10]:

web_blocks.takeaway: Rear axle shafts generate nearly three-quarters of total revenue (~74.3%), while ICRA's November 13, 2026 rationale shows FY26 regional sales split 56% Asia, 18% North America, 13% South America, and 13% Europe (~53% Domestic / ~47% Export)—exposing exports to dual-layer U.S. trade policy alongside India's tractor cycle [10][30][33].

web_blocks.title: Segment 1: Rear Axle Shafts (~74.3% of Revenue) — Concrete End-to-End Example

web_blocks.html: A rear axle shaft is a solid forged steel bar inside the rear axle housing. It has an upset-forged wheel flange at one end and precision splines at the other. When the differential splits engine torque, the shaft twists to turn the rear wheels. It also bears vertical and cornering shock loads [6].

Concrete Real-World Example (North American Class 8 Truck Axle Shaft): Picture a heavy-duty Class 8 tractor-trailer running on US Interstate 80. Freightliner or Kenworth builds the truck around a tandem drive axle from Dana or Cummins-Meritor [11][16]. That rig hauls 80,000 pounds (36 tonnes) over mountain grades in sub-zero winters and desert heat. Dana cannot risk a torsional fatigue crack at the spline root. Under multi-year contracts, GNA buys certified micro-alloy steel bars and shears them to length at Mehtiana. Workers heat the bar ends and use horizontal upsetters and Lasco extrusion presses to form the wheel flange in one continuous grain-flow [7][24]. Next, CNC lathes turn the shaft and cut or roll the splines. In-house induction lines then harden the outer skin while keeping the core ductile and shock-resistant [7][24]. After 100% magnetic-particle crack checks, GNA rust-proofs and packs the shafts in containers. Ships carry them from Mundra or Nhava Sheva to Dana's North American plants, billed in USD with alloy-steel price pass-through [11][16]. Notably, U.S.-bound medium- and heavy-duty truck parts have faced a 25% U.S. Section 232 tariff since November 1, 2025; while USTR's November 25, 2026 Section 301 notice proposes exempting Section 232-covered truck parts from additional duty stacking, USMCA/Mexican peers still benefit from non-U.S.-content carve-outs [30][31].

web_blocks.title: Segment 2: Spindles (~17.2% of Revenue) — Concrete End-to-End Example

web_blocks.html: Unlike a rotating drive shaft, a spindle (or stub axle) does not spin. It is a high-strength forged steel journal bolted or welded to the steering knuckle or trailer beam. Wheel hub bearings ride directly on its ground journals. That means the spindle carries the vehicle's full static and cornering weight [6].

Concrete Real-World Example (Global Agricultural Tractor & Off-Highway Spindle): Picture a 75-to-120 HP row-crop tractor built by John Deere or Kubota working muddy fields in Iowa, Brazil, or Punjab [11][17]. When the tractor turns hard with a loaded front bucket or raised rotavator, heavy bending shear hits the front spindle shoulder. At Gulabgarh Jattan, GNA drop-forges alloy steel billets into near-net spindle shapes. Continuous carburizing furnaces heat-treat the parts to prevent brittle fracture, and grinders finish the bearing seats to micron tolerances [7][24]. Priced per piece with steel pass-through clauses, these spindles ship straight to John Deere's global axle lines. GNA holds single-source or dual-source status on many of those part numbers [5][17]. However, off-highway agricultural and construction spindles exported to U.S. plants sit outside Section 232 on-highway vehicle exemptions and therefore face direct exposure to USTR's November 25, 2026 proposed 25% Section 301 tariff on Indian goods (17% if India concludes a reciprocal trade deal), with public comments due January 5, 2027 [30][31].

web_blocks.title: Segment 3: Drive Shafts, Splined Shafts & The New SUV/EV Expansion (~8.5% of Revenue)

web_blocks.html: The third pillar covers drive shafts, PTO (power take-off) shafts, and splined transmission shafts. It makes up ~8.5% of historical sales, but it anchors GNA's push into SUVs and electric vehicles [10][22]. Legacy Class 8 shafts are heavy (30–165 kg) and cyclical. By contrast, SUVs, pickups, and EVs need lighter, tighter-tolerance half-shafts and e-axle rotor shafts built for instant electric torque [6][22].

Concrete Real-World Example (Domestic Tractor PTO & Light-Vehicle/SUV Shafts): On a 50-HP Mahindra or TAFE tractor in Madhya Pradesh, a GNA PTO drive shaft sends engine power out the back at 540 RPM to run a thresher or rotavator [11]. Meanwhile, GNA's light-vehicle and SUV line is tracking above a ₹240 Cr FY27 annual run-rate (well ahead of an earlier ₹150 Cr target), while management has deployed ₹40 Cr of an ₹80 Cr EV and allied shaft capex tranche—with a further ₹40 Cr planned over the next 6–8 months through its wholly owned subsidiary GNA Mobility Limited (note: a June 8, 2026 exchange corrigendum confirmed GNA Mobility's investment plan is ₹80 Cr, correcting an ₹800 Cr misprint in the FY26 Annual Report) [4][22][38]. Across Mehtiana (~1.2M off-highway components/yr) and Gulabgarh Jattan (up to ~5.0M PV/CV/spindle components/yr), installed capacity has expanded to ~6.2–6.7 million parts per year [6][22].

web_blocks.takeaway: GNA's secret to surviving FY24–FY26 without margin collapse was its two-legged stool: domestic tractors held the floor when US Class 8 trucks slowed, while the emerging SUV/EV line adds a third leg even as dual U.S. Section 232 and proposed Section 301 tariffs reshape export economics [5][22][30][31].

book_paragraphs: If you walked onto the shop floor of GNA's Mehtiana plant tomorrow morning, you would not see consumer gadgets or finished trucks. You would see glowing orange billets of alloy steel being slammed inside German-built Lasco extrusion presses and horizontal upsetters [7][24]. GNA Axles is a specialist's specialist: roughly 74.3% of its revenue comes from rear axle shafts, 17.2% from spindles, and 8.5% from drive and splined shafts [10]. Across Mehtiana (~1.2 million off-highway parts/yr) and Gulabgarh Jattan (up to 5.0 million PV, CV, and spindle parts/yr), total installed capacity now spans roughly 6.2 to 6.7 million precision-forged components per year, with FY26 sales split 56% Asia, 18% North America, 13% South America, and 13% Europe per ICRA's November 13, 2026 credit rationale [11][33].

Let us make each segment concrete so you can picture the economics—and the tariff friction. Start with Rear Axle Shafts, the three-quarter heavyweight of the business. Picture a 36-tonne Class 8 Freightliner truck hauling freight across the Rocky Mountains, built on a tandem drive axle engineered by Dana or Cummins-Meritor [11][16]. Inside that axle housing sit two solid forged steel shafts made in Punjab. GNA shears certified alloy steel bars, upset-forges the wheel flange so the metal's grain flow never breaks, CNC-machines the splines, induction-hardens the surface, and ships those 30-to-65 kg shafts across the ocean to Dana's North American assembly lines [7][11][24]. Since November 1, 2025, those U.S.-bound medium- and heavy-duty truck parts have operated under a 25% Section 232 tariff; USTR's November 25, 2026 Section 301 proposal carves out Section 232 auto and truck parts from double-stacking, but leaves USMCA/Mexican peers with a persistent duty edge [30][31].

Next, look at Spindles—17.2% of sales [10]. Unlike a spinning axle shaft, a spindle is a stationary stub axle that carries the entire vertical and cornering load of a wheel hub. Picture a 100-horsepower John Deere or Kubota tractor churning through wet clay in Iowa or Brazil [11][17]. Every time the operator whips the steering wheel with a loaded front bucket, shear force concentrates on that spindle. GNA drop-forges, carburizes, and micron-grinds those spindles at Gulabgarh Jattan so they never snap under shock loads [7][24]. Crucially, any off-highway agricultural or construction spindles exported into the United States outside Section 232 vehicle classifications now face direct exposure to USTR's November 25, 2026 proposed 25% Section 301 tariff on Indian goods (17% if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement) [30][31].

Finally, look at Drive Shafts and the fast-growing SUV and EV-allied vertical (8.5% historical share, now scaling rapidly) [10][22]. On a domestic Mahindra or TAFE tractor, GNA's PTO drive shaft spins farm implements behind the cab [11]. More importantly, GNA is dedicating ₹80 crore of targeted EV/allied capex—₹40 crore already deployed by Q2 FY27 and ₹40 crore slated over the next 6–8 months alongside wholly owned subsidiary GNA Mobility Limited (clarified at ₹80 crore via a June 8, 2026 BSE corrigendum after an ₹800 crore Annual Report misprint)—toward lighter 1.5-to-10 kg splined and rotor shafts for passenger SUVs and electric powertrains, pushing its light-vehicle revenue run-rate past ₹240 crore [4][6][22][38]. That three-legged mix—global trucks, tractors, and SUV/EV platforms—keeps GNA's furnaces running around 80% utilization today [22].

book_subsections.title: How the Two-Legged Stool Cushioned FY24–FY26—and the Third Leg Now Scaling
paragraphs: You can see why GNA's geography mix—56% Asia, 18% North America, 13% South America, and 13% Europe in FY26 (~53% domestic and ~47% export)—matters so much when you examine the FY24–FY26 slowdown [10][33]. When North American Class 8 heavy-truck builds cooled and U.S. Section 232 tariff uncertainty froze distributor restocking, export volumes took a hit [5][31]. Yet domestic Indian tractor and off-highway demand stayed resilient, keeping Mehtiana and Gulabgarh Jattan running without a single quarter of operating losses [1][5].

Now management is adding a third leg: light vehicles, SUVs, and EV-allied shafts. By Q2 FY27, GNA had already deployed ₹40 crore out of an earmarked ₹80 crore EV/allied capex tranche (coordinated alongside subsidiary GNA Mobility Limited), while light-vehicle and SUV shaft sales were scaling past a ₹240 crore annual run-rate [4][22][38]. These smaller 1.5-to-10 kg shafts require tighter CNC tolerances and run on dedicated cells, giving GNA a vital counterweight to North American truck cyclicality and November 2026 U.S. Section 301 tariff risk over FY27–FY29 [6][22][30].

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Boring Safety-Critical Parts Beat Sexy Aftermarket Brands
book_callouts.text: At first glance, forging steel shafts sounds like a low-tech commodity business. Look closer: a rear axle shaft represents a tiny fraction of a Class 8 truck's total build cost, yet a single field failure triggers a catastrophic highway accident and a multi-million-dollar OEM recall. That asymmetry—low cost to the OEM, catastrophic cost of failure—explains why Dana, Meritor, and John Deere stick with qualified suppliers like GNA for decades rather than switching for a 2% price cut [5][11]. The real question for Chapter 3 is how much working capital GNA must lock up to service those global giants.
